applies_why: The judge text makes an UNDERDETERMINED ruling on Isaiah 7:14 because the sign's sense is left open, which is the kind of single-verse/open-sense ground K-S2 governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: I weighed 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand' against the judge's 'leaving the sign's sense open': one reading forbids calling the sign open when it has two senses, while the other would make the open-sign statement an unresolved single-verse basis, which K-S2 also bars.
why: The judge labels D5 vs C5 UNDERDETERMINED because the sign's sense is left open, but K-S2 forbids using a single verse's silence or a verse's two senses as an open/UNDERDETERMINED ground.
